blocks.text: LOG:000–022 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The Logic entity block was reconsidered from first principles under the standing delegated authority. The review compared five genuinely different architectures per root, scored 45 candidates across 360 criterion values, routed 126 English concepts without forced atomization, passed all 18 canonical packet checks, passed all 19 dedicated Logic entity-layer soundness checks, and passed the complete authority regression. All deterministic generated forms remained unchanged.

Approved architecture: LOG:0xx names substrate-neutral formal constraint entities. The inward triplet names one formal criterion within a reference entity’s logical specification; the outward triplet names one formal constraint assigned to one distinct target; and the systemic triplet names one correlated formal regime across multiple participants in a shared rule domain. The third trit changes only persistent, operative, or dormant status.

LOG:000 — persistent internal formal criterion — A persistent formal criterion within the logical specification of one reference entity that limits that entity's admissible states independently of whether the criterion is presently operative.
LOG:001 — operative internal formal criterion — A formal criterion within the logical specification of one reference entity that is presently operative in limiting that entity's admissible states.

LOG:002 — dormant internal formal criterion — A formal criterion within the logical specification of one reference entity that remains defined without presently operating to limit that entity's admissible states.

LOG:010 — persistent target-directed formal constraint — A persistent formal constraint assigned to one distinct reference target that limits the target's admissible states independently of whether the constraint is presently operative.
LOG:011 — operative target-directed formal constraint — A formal constraint assigned to one distinct reference target that is presently operative in limiting the target's admissible states.

LOG:012 — dormant target-directed formal constraint — A formal constraint assigned to one distinct reference target that remains defined without presently operating to limit the target's admissible states.

LOG:020 — persistent shared formal regime — A persistent formal regime that correlates admissibility criteria across multiple participants in one shared rule domain independently of whether the regime is presently operative.
LOG:021 — operative shared formal regime — A formal regime that is presently operative in correlating admissibility criteria across multiple participants in one shared rule domain.

LOG:022 — dormant shared formal regime — A formal regime that remains defined across multiple participants in one shared rule domain without presently operating to correlate their admissibility criteria.

Design boundary: these roots do not silently encode proposition truth or falsity; assertion or belief; represented values, variables, bindings, records, schemas, or code; satisfaction, violation, validity, proof, inference, evaluation, or execution; authorship, institutional authority, enforcement, or sanction; physical or domain mechanisms; applicability, entailment, consistency, computability, time, or modality. Persistent rule identity may co-occur with operative or dormant status; operative and dormant are mutually exclusive for the same rule at one reference time. Lexical dormancy remains distinct from runtime [2]/num uncertainty.
